items.title: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon
items.oneliner: Google says Gemini 4 Argon beats frontier rivals and already optimizes code and datacenters internally, so deployment is the real story.

items.title: OpenAI expanded its agent stack
items.oneliner: OpenAI bundled computer use, Decisions API, and persistent agents, pushing developers from chat apps toward full workflow automation.

items.title: Border phone searches face a challenge
items.oneliner: A new lawsuit targets warrantless CBP phone searches, reminding teams that sensitive data on employee devices is still exposed.

items.title: Mathematicians warned on AI-generated proofs
items.oneliner: Researchers are calling for responsible release of AI-generated math, because unreadable proofs are useless if nobody can verify them.

items.title: Netlify rebuilt edge execution
items.oneliner: Netlify moved Edge Functions from isolates to Firecracker microVMs and cut warm latency to 5-6 ms from 25-40 ms.

items.title: Magnitude targets faster local inference
items.oneliner: Magnitude claims up to 2x llama.cpp performance by compiling kernels per device, which matters if agents are moving on-device.

items.title: OpenAI partnered with Synopsys
items.oneliner: OpenAI and Synopsys are building a chip-design model, a sign that domain-specific copilots are heading into hard engineering.

items.title: EDG opened its C++ front end
items.oneliner: EDG's 30-year-old C++ front end is going public, giving compiler and tooling teams a serious new open foundation.

items.title: OpenDLSS recreated Nvidia neural rendering
items.oneliner: An open Vulkan reimplementation of DLSS 5 suggests proprietary neural graphics stacks may be reverse-engineered faster than expected.

items.title: Multi-Wi-Fi streaming showed real gains
items.oneliner: NanoPing delivered zero packet loss and 49 ms max delay by bonding Wi-Fi links, which is practical infrastructure, not AI theater.
